transcript.text: What’s the dress code?

For the events during the Opening Week, the dress code is generally casual or business casual. However, for the Outdoor Campus event, it's best to wear something sporty and comfortable since we'll be getting our hands dirty with outdoor activities. And don't forget to pick up your First-Year T-shirt at the event! 🎽😊 If you're heading to the Semester Opening party at Gateway Gardens, the dress code is "Ibiza vibes," so feel free to bring out your stylish summer attire! 🌴🎉 Let me know if you need any more info!
Opening ceremony

The Opening Ceremony is the grand event marking the official start of your academic journey at FS. It takes place today, August 30th, from 17:00 to 21:00. 🎉 During the ceremony, you'll be formally welcomed by university leaders and faculty members. It's a fantastic opportunity to meet fellow students from various programs and start forming connections with your peers. The atmosphere will be filled with excitement and energy, setting the tone for the year ahead. Remember, Frankie will send you a ticket on the morning of the event, which can be used by you and your guests. If you haven't received it yet, don't worry! Just head to the Trouble Desk when you arrive at the campus, and they'll sort everything out for you. Enjoy the ceremony and the beginning of this exciting chapter! 😊
Suit and tie expected?

For the Opening Ceremony, a suit and tie are not required. The dress code is generally casual or business casual, so you can choose something comfortable yet presentable. Feel free to express your personal style while keeping it classy! Enjoy the event and have a fantastic time connecting with everyone. 😊
Isn’t that to informal?

I totally get where you're coming from! While the dress code is generally casual or business casual, some students do opt for a more formal look like a suit and tie, especially for such an important event. It's really up to you and what makes you feel comfortable and confident. If dressing up a bit more feels right for you, go for it! The key is to enjoy the ceremony and make the most of this special occasion. 😊
